evidence.locator: ACR Clinical Image Testing: Mammography — For all submissions; initial/renewal requirements; reviewer scoring
evidence.claim: For ACR mammography accreditation, each submitted exam is the CC and MLO views of both breasts (four images from one patient). Initial or renewal submissions include one fatty-breast exam and one dense-breast exam, and at least two ACR radiologist reviewers score eight image-quality parameters. ACR points to the Clinical Image Evaluation section of its 1999 QC manual for the detailed review criteria.

evidence.locator: ACR Learning Network — Mammography Positioning Review Guidelines Table — Major: CC posterior tissue, breast cut off; Minor: CC exaggeration
evidence.claim: On the CC, posterior tissue (typically the retroglandular fat plane) should be on the image; the pectoralis muscle is visible on the CC in roughly 30% of women. Medial or lateral tissue cut off on the CC is a failure. Ideally the nipple is centered near midline; exaggeration that moves the nipple off midline and loses medial or lateral posterior tissue is excessive.
evidence.scope: Technologist evaluation of standard screening views. Teaches what to check, not hands-on correction maneuvers.

evidence.locator: ACR Learning Network — Mammography Positioning Review Guidelines Table — Minor criteria: MLO amount of pectoralis major muscle
evidence.claim: On the MLO, the pectoralis should reach down to the PNL or below and be wider at the top, gradually narrowing toward the bottom. evidence.locator: ACR Learning Network — Mammography Positioning Review Guidelines Table — Minor criteria: MLO IMF, sagging, detector position; Major: motion, other body parts
evidence.claim: On the MLO, the inframammary fold should be open without folds; a closed or excluded IMF, or large folds hiding tissue, is inadequate. The breast should be lifted rather than sagging and centered on the detector; positioning too high shows too much abdomen and not enough axilla. Across views there should be no motion and no other body part (chin, hand, shoulder, opposite breast) over the breast.

evidence.locator: PMC9562663 (Brahim et al. 2022) — 2.1 Mediolateral-Oblique View; 3.2 MLO: Pectoralis Muscle Level
evidence.claim: The MLO shows the upper outer quadrant with the greatest amount of breast tissue. An adequate MLO has a relaxed pectoralis imaged to nipple level that is convex or straight (angle of at least about 10°), the nipple in profile, all breast tissue including retroglandular fat, and no skin folds. The lower pectoralis edge should be at or below the PNL, drawn from the nipple perpendicular to the pectoralis line.
evidence.scope: Technologist evaluation of standard screening views. Teaches what to check, not hands-on correction maneuvers.

evidence.locator: ACR BI-RADS Mammography v2025, Appendix B summary form (manual pp.173–176) — A. Masses
evidence.claim: A mass is three-dimensional and occupies space: it is seen on two different projections (or consecutive DBT slices) and has a wholly or partly convex-outward contour. v2025 shape terms are oval, lobulated, round, and irregular. Margin terms are circumscribed (at least 75% sharply demarcated), obscured (25% or more hidden by overlapping tissue, visible part circumscribed), indistinct, and spiculated (lines radiating from the mass). Density terms compare the mass with an equal volume of fibroglandular tissue: fat-containing, low, equal, or high.
evidence.scope: Technologist recognition of lexicon terms. Radiologists apply descriptors and assessments; this is not interpretation training.

evidence.locator: ACR BI-RADS Mammography v2025, Appendix B summary form (manual pp.173–176) — B.1 Typically benign; B.2 Suspicious morphology
evidence.claim: Calcification morphology is split into typically benign and suspicious. v2025 typically benign terms: skin, vascular, coarse, large rod-like, round, rim, layering, and suture. Suspicious morphology terms: amorphous (too small or hazy to define a shape), coarse heterogeneous (irregular, about 0.5–1 mm, tending to coalesce), fine pleomorphic (discrete varied shapes, usually under 0.5 mm), and fine linear or fine linear-branching (thin linear forms under 0.5 mm, sometimes branching).
evidence.scope: Technologist recognition of lexicon terms. Radiologists apply descriptors and assessments; this is not interpretation training.

evidence.locator: ACR BI-RADS Mammography v2025, Appendix B summary form (manual pp.173–176) — B.3 Distribution
evidence.claim: Calcification distribution terms are diffuse (random throughout the breast), regional (a large area over 2 cm, not following a duct), grouped (relatively few calcifications in a small area, generally at least 5 within 1 cm or more within 2 cm), linear (arranged in a line), and segmental (suggesting deposits in a duct and its branches, often a triangle pointing toward the nipple).

evidence.locator: ACR BI-RADS Mammography v2025, Appendix B summary form (manual pp.173–176) — C. Architectural distortion; D. Asymmetries
evidence.claim: Architectural distortion means the parenchyma is distorted with no definite mass visible. Asymmetries are unilateral fibroglandular-density deposits that do not meet the mass definition: an asymmetry is seen on only one projection and often reflects superimposed normal tissue; a focal asymmetry is seen on more than one view, covers less than a quadrant, and has a concave-outward contour usually mixed with fat; a global asymmetry covers at least a quadrant.
